SMTO-WEB-0009 — SMTO can't unpack the way this site sent the page

GUID: bd3a2e79-b1fe-448d-994c-e569cee5a0b6
Slug: web-unsupported-content-encoding
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • The website sent the page squeezed in a format SMTO's web reader can't unpack safely. SMTO didn't try to read the scrambled data, so nothing was read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Give SMTO a different address with the same information, such as a plain-text, print or PDF version of the page. A different page from the site may be sent in a packed format SMTO can unpack.
  2. If the Browser Skill is available in your conversation, ask SMTO to open the page with the Browser instead. The Browser opens pages the way a normal web browser does, so it can handle formats the web reader can't.
  3. If you only need part of the page, open it in your own browser, copy the text you need and paste it into your message. Your own browser can unpack the page, and SMTO can then work with the text directly.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the page's content from the new address or tool.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the address, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't let anyone treat the unreadable data as the page's text.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Web reader rejected the response because its Content-Encoding is not identity, gzip or deflate, or extra compressed data followed a supported stream.

What this means

  • The reader rejects an unsupported content encoding or extra compressed data after a supported stream. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • The reader rejects an unsupported content encoding or extra compressed data after a supported stream.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Content-Encoding and the exact decoder failure without treating undecoded bytes as text.

How to fix it

  • read_body in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/transport.py and documents.acquire accept only identity, gzip/x-gzip or deflate, and reject stacked streams (decoder.unused_data). The request sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, so the origin ignored it (for example sent br); use another URL for the content or a supported HTTP or Browser route.
  • Request a supported encoding or use a supported native HTTP/file route.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported single encoding yields a complete bounded body.

What not to do

  • Do not interpret encoded bytes as decoded page text.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
